description:
Choose which browser opens every link.

LinkUnbound puts itself between a link and your browsers, so every link opens where you
want it. It becomes the default handler for http and https, and when a link arrives it
asks which browser — or answers on its own, from a rule you taught it. Rules remember
the choices you make, by site, by profile or by the program the link came from. Work in
one browser and personal in another, without moving a default back and forth. Everything
stays on your machine: no account, no telemetry, no server.
v2.12.0
Until now every update waited for you to press Update on the picker, so a
LinkUnbound you never pressed it on stayed behind.
- LinkUnbound can now install its updates on its own. Turn on «Install updates
  on their own» in Settings, Application. It starts off, waits until the
  picker is out of sight, and LinkUnbound restarts by itself afterwards.
- The picker asks you once with each new version whether updates may install
  on their own. Answer yes, not now, or don't ask again.
- A copy from the Microsoft Store keeps updating through the Store, and is
  never asked.
- If an update fails, the picker and Settings offer to download the new
  version from the web, opened in the browser you chose for GitHub or in
  your first one.
What's Changed
- feat(updater): a spare key built into the app verifies the releases it signed by @rgdevment in #111
- feat(updates): updates can install on their own, chosen in Settings and asked once a minor version on the picker by @rgdevment in #112
- feat(news): what 2.12.0 brings, updates that install on their own by @rgdevment in #113
- feat(updates): a failed update offers to download it from the web, in the rule's browser or the first one by @rgdevment in #114
Full Changelog: v2.11.0...v2.12.0
